name: Centralized And Decentralized Reputation Allocate Evaluation Differently
text:
Evaluative authority has an institutional location. Noorian and Ulieru classify centralized reputation systems by a central database and authority that receive transaction reports, aggregate ratings, and calculate public scores. Their decentralized category removes that location. Each agent stores ratings and uses a tailored computation engine to calculate and validate the trustworthiness of a potential partner.

This classification independently extends Kaal's distinction. A centralized reward model and cohort-governed reputation do not merely apply different techniques to the same evaluator. They allocate the collection, computation, and validation of evaluative information to different actors.

The correspondence is limited. Noorian and Ulieru study trust and reputation systems in online communities and open multi-agent systems. They do not analyze reward modeling, Kaal's cohort design, deliberation, or reputation-bearing consequences. Their framework supports the institutional allocation claim. It does not establish the comparative accuracy, legitimacy, or resistance to manipulation of either design in Kaal's setting.

sourceEvidencePassages.text: In centralized reputation systems, information about the QoS of a particular SP is stored in a central database. For this reason, after every transaction agents are asked to report the performance of their transaction partners to a central authority. The accumulated ratings are evaluated using an employed reputation calculation engine to derive the expected reputation score for every participant and then make them publicly available [9].

locator.version: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research 5(2)

sourceEvidencePassages.text: In a decentralized reputation system there is no central location for submitting the transaction feedback and for querying the expected reputation score of a particular destination agent [9]. Instead, each agent is capable of storing the ratings locally and manipulates them when required. Moreover, in this approach participants are equipped with the reputation computation engines tailored to their demands so as to calculate and validate the trustfulness of their transaction partners.
